subject: Re: MAP update & timing — procurement review may shift close
messages:
From: John Waverly <john.waverly@acmecorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: procurement review may push close out ~3 weeks

Hi Naomi,

Quick heads up from our side: legal & procurement just flagged an extra compliance review on our data retention appendix. Procurement says they need an extra 2–3 weeks to finish signatures and internal approvals.

That would likely move our original close date out by ~3 weeks. We're still committed to the integration and the evaluation plan, but the timing is shifting. Can you and your team share a lean MAP that shows:
- which milestones are flexible vs. hard (go-live cutover date vs. internal procurement & billing),
- minimal acceptance criteria for an early canary,
- fallbacks so we can start limited testing before full signature?

If you send a short traffic-light plan (green/amber/red) that maps the steps we can present internally, I can push it through procurement.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

John
John Waverly
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Attachments: none (procurement referenced internal doc)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: John Waverly <john.waverly@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: procurement review may push close out ~3 weeks

Hi John —

Thanks for the callout. I've sketched a lightweight traffic-light MAP that separates procurement/billing milestones from technical acceptance:

GREEN:
- Contract signed + PO submitted -> full provisioning + onboarding (target close)
- Acceptance criteria: production-like workload pass for 24h, SLO targets met (p99 < 200ms)

AMBER (can start before signatures):
- Limited canary window (2 weeks) with restricted volume and isolated dataset
- Pre-signed MSA or interim T&Cs + procurement memo to enable test invoices
- Acceptance criteria: functional validation on sample workflows, basic perf metrics

RED (blocking):
- Legal needs changes to data retention or customer data egress -> requires updated SOW
- If red, no canary until legal sign-off

Options to accelerate:
- We can provision a dedicated test slice immediately (no PO required) for a paid pilot — Marissa, can ops reserve a 1-GPU canary pool?
- If procurement needs a softer deadline, we can offer a conditional SLA credit during the first 30 days after go-live to reduce procurement friction.

I've attached a short MAP spreadsheet (MAP_v1.2.xlsx) with the milestones and suggested owners. If that looks good, I'll do a tightened MAP_v1.3 that includes the canary gating and DocuSign link.

Call to action for Acme: confirm which milestone you can move to AMBER (allowing canary) and whether procurement will accept a conditional invoice path or needs a PO in hand.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0124

Attachment: MAP_v1.2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: procurement review may push close out ~3 weeks

Internal note — quick options and constraints from ops/product:

1) Canary capacity
- We can carve a 1-GPU canary pool for Acme (limited qps) immediately. No PO needed for provisioning, but billing needs a temporary cost-acceptance note.

2) Feature gating and monitoring
- Karthik: can we restrict features (no external tool-calls) for the canary to lower legal risk?
- Priyom: prepare a minimal eval dashboard and token cost cap to prevent runaway charges during the pilot.

3) SLA/credit
- We can offer a small credit tied to on-time go-live if procurement needs an economic incentive. Finance will need a signed MSA to apply credits post-fact.

Risks
- If legal changes data-retention clauses it becomes a hard stop. Escalation path: Naomi + Marissa to file an exceptions request with Security & Legal (24–48h triage).

I'll hold the canary pool for 72 hours pending confirmation from Naomi.

Marissa
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: John Waverly <john.waverly@acmecorp.com>, Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: procurement review may push close out ~3 weeks

John / Lisa —

Appreciate the quick read on procurement. Per Marissa and product, attached is MAP_v1.3 with a recommended Traffic-Light Action Plan and an explicit canary path so Acme can begin verification before full signature. Highlights:

- Canary window (AMBER): 2-week limited throughput slice (1 GPU), isolated dataset, feature-gate applied.
- Acceptance for canary: pass of 5 core test flows, no P0 defects, perf within amber thresholds (p95 < 350ms).
- Escalation: if legal requests new retention controls, we will pause canary and escalate to Security (target 48h response).
- Commercials: conditional invoice path (pilot invoice for the canary) documented; DocuSign SOW link included so procurement can route quickly.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/XYZ-ACME-2027 (attached as DocuSign_acme_SOW_link.txt)

Please confirm: 1) Acme accepts the AMBER canary path, 2) expected date procurement can sign the SOW (tentative date), and 3) any legal clauses that would remain blocking.

If you say yes to the canary we will: reserve the pool, schedule an onboarding session this week, and spin up the eval dashboard.

Onward —
Naomi
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v1.3.xlsx, DocuSign_acme_SOW_link.txt

This is exactly what procurement needed to see. We accept the AMBER canary path and will route the DocuSign SOW through procurement with a target of 2027-04-30 for signatures. Procurement has agreed to a conditional invoice for the pilot as long as legal doesn't change retention clauses.

Next steps:
- I will confirm the exact signature date by Tue (20 Apr).
- Lisa will coordinate a kickoff for the canary (we'd like an onboarding call next Wed).

Thanks to you and your team for the quick turnaround — this traffic-light structure will help unstick the internal review.
